newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DUTCH TREAT FOR BLOOMSDAY AT SUMMIT.
newsitem.headline: DUTCH TREAT FOR BLOOMSDAY AT SUMMIT.

text.p: Dutch fans of James Joyce's "Ulysses" got a special treat because of the European Union summit on Monday as a stream of Irish visitors and dignitaries joined in the annual Bloomsday celebration in Amsterdam.
Irish Foreign Minister Dick Spring, Ireland's ambassador to the Netherlands John Swift and visiting Irish Times journalist Denis Staunton kicked off the day-long reading of Joyce's masterpiece.
"Ulysses" tells the tale of one day -- June 16 -- in the life of Leopold Bloom in Dublin. Fans hold gatherings all over the world every year on the day to celebrate the book with a marathon reading.
